references.text: The penalty for idolatry and offering sacrifices to gods other than the Lord was death, which explains why the people demanded Gideon's execution for destroying Baal's altar.
Mosaic law commanded that those who led others into idolatry should be put to death. The men of the city applied this logic in reverse against Gideon, who had removed idolatry.
The procedure for capital punishment required witnesses and a legal trial, which the men of the city sought to carry out against Gideon.
Elijah killed Baal's prophets on Mount Carmel, a parallel action against Baal worship that Gideon also confronted.
Jezebel threatened Elijah with death for killing Baal's prophets, just as the men of the city demanded Gideon's execution for destroying Baal's altar.
The immediate context in which Gideon tore down Baal's altar and the Asherah pole, leading the men of the city to demand his death.
